record.title: The 3-daisy density conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal D_3$ be the daisy formed from a fixed $1$-set and a disjoint $4$-set, and let $\pi(\mathcal D_3)$ be its limiting Turán density. **The 3-daisy density conjecture.**

$$
\pi(\mathcal D_3)=\frac12.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by iterating blow-ups of the complement of the Fano plane, which yields density $1/2$; the source states that the exact limiting density was not known.
record.source_name: Bela Bollobas, Imre Leader and Claudia Malvenuto, “Daisies and Other Turan Problems”, arXiv:1105.1553 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1553

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2011).

record.title: The 1089 graph characterization by endpoint digits
record.statement:
Let $N=(a_{n-1}\binom{\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!}{\vphantom{1}}\cdots a_0)_g$ be a $(g,k)$-reverse multiple, with endpoint digits $a_0$ and $a_{n-1}$, and let its associated graph be the **Young graph**. The **1089 graph** is the Young graph isomorphic to the $(10,4)$ and $(10,9)$ Young graphs.

**1089 graph endpoint conjecture.** If there is a $(g,k)$-reverse multiple with $a_0+a_{n-1}=g$, then the Young graph is the 1089 graph. Conversely, if the graph is the 1089 graph, then every reverse multiple satisfies $a_0+a_{n-1}=g$.

The first implication is suggested by the preceding theorem together with the 1089 graph conjecture, while the converse is also expected to follow from that conjecture. The claim is stated separately because it may have an independent proof and is used later in the paper.
record.source_name: N. J. A. Sloane, “2178 And All That”, arXiv:1307.0453 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.0453

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2013).

record.title: Solvability conjecture for mazes whose origin component is a path
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be the subset of square-lattice mazes in which the connected component of the origin is a simple, possibly infinite, path. **Path-component maze solvability conjecture.** There exists an algorithm that solves $\mathcal{N}$. The paper presents this as a further positive result expected to hold; no proof or resolution is supplied, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Stefan David and Marius Tiba, “Solvability of Mazes by Blind Robots”, arXiv:1804.05439 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.05439

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: Füredi's conjecture for blowups of the 4-cycle
record.statement:
For $r\geq 3$, let

$$
\mathcal{C}_4^r:=\{C_4(a,b):a+b=r,\ a,b>0\}.
$$

**Füredi's conjecture.** The extremal number satisfies

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{C}_4^r)\sim \binom{n}{r-1}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the extremal density of all $(a,b)$-blowups of a 4-cycle and is attributed in the paper to Füredi; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, Tao Jiang, Alexandr Kostochka, Dhruv Mubayi and Jacques Verstraëte, “Extremal problems for hypergraph blowups of trees”, arXiv:2003.00622 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.00622

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

record.title: Odd density conjecture for residue classes of 21-regular partitions
record.statement:
Let $b_{21}(n)$ be the number of $21$-regular partitions of $n$.

**Odd density conjecture for $b_{21}$.** The series

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_{21}(4n+2)q^n
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_{21}(4n+3)q^n
$$

have odd density $1/2$. Consequently, the $21$-regular partition function has odd density $1/4$.

The preceding arguments establish lacunarity modulo $2$ for the residue classes $4n$ and $4n+1$, while this conjecture predicts the contrasting density-$1/2$ behavior of the other two classes. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: William J. Keith and Fabrizio Zanello, “Parity of the coefficients of certain eta-quotients”, arXiv:2010.09881 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.09881

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2020). “In the final section, we offer some concluding remarks, including applications to other classes of eta-quotients, and present further open questions that might be of interest for future investigations.”

record.title: Conjecture on the relative difference-index bound
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with sum index $\operatorname{sum}(G)$ and difference index $\operatorname{dif}(G)$. **Relative difference-index bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{dif}(G)\leq\operatorname{sum}(G).
$$

The text presents this as an expected extension of the known result for bipartite graphs. Its resolution is not given in the supplied passage.
record.source_name: John Haslegrave, “Sum index, difference index and exclusive sum number of graphs”, arXiv:2104.06959 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06959

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Rank and crank log-concavity conjectures
record.statement:
Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote respectively the number of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$. **Rank and crank log-concavity conjecture.** The inequalities

$$
M(m,n)^2\ge M(m-1,n)M(m+1,n)
$$

hold for $n\ge71$ and $|m|\le n-71$, and

$$
N(m,n)^2\ge N(m-1,n)N(m+1,n)
$$

hold for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$. These conjectures motivate the paper's generalization to Garvan $k$-rank statistics.
record.source_name: Nian Hong Zhou, “Eventual log-concavity of k-rank statistics for integer partitions”, arXiv:2110.11174 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.11174

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Hussain–Niepel–Kinawi's optimal LPDS density conjecture for king grids
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be the infinite king grid with vertex set $V=\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$, in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when their Euclidean distance is at most $\sqrt{2}$. For a set $S\subseteq V$, define its density by

$$
D(S)=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\frac{|S\cap N_G^k[u]|}{|N_G^k[u]|},
$$

where $N_G^k[u]=\{x\in V(G)\mid d(u,x)\leq k\}$ and $d(u,x)$ is graph distance. An **optimal locating-paired-dominating set** (optimal LPDS) is an LPDS of minimal density. **Hussain–Niepel–Kinawi's conjecture.** If $S$ is an optimal LPDS in the king grid and $D(S)$ is its density, then

$$
D(S)=\frac{2}{9}.
$$

Previously, the density of an optimal LPDS was known to satisfy $3/14\leq D(S)\leq 2/9$; the conjecture asserts that the upper bound is attained and hence determines the optimal density exactly.
record.source_name: Yuxuan Yang, “Optimal Locating-Paired-Dominating Sets in King Grids”, arXiv:2210.11838 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11838

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

record.title: Krivelevich–Sudakov Hamiltonicity conjecture for pseudorandom graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an **$(n,d,\lambda)$-graph**, meaning an $n$-vertex $d$-regular graph whose non-trivial eigenvalues have absolute value at most $\lambda$. A **Hamilton cycle** is a cycle containing every vertex of $G$. **Krivelevich and Sudakov's conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $C$ such that, if

$$
\frac{d}{\lambda}\ge C,
$$

then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle.

This conjecture asks for a spectral-gap condition guaranteeing Hamiltonicity in pseudorandom graphs. The paper presents it as a conjecture posed nearly 20 years ago; no resolution is supplied in the provided context.
record.source_name: Matías Pavez-Signé, “Spanning trees in the square of pseudorandom graphs”, arXiv:2307.00322 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2205.15228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15228).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00322

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

record.title: Bowler–Brown–Fenner tree-recognition conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let a **card** be an unlabeled vertex-deleted subgraph $G-v$. **Bowler–Brown–Fenner conjecture.** For $n\geq 44$, it can be determined whether $G$ is a tree from any $\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor+2$ of its cards. The conjecture gives the expected sharp number of cards needed to recognize trees from incomplete decks; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Gabriëlle Zwaneveld, “Recognizing trees from incomplete decks”, arXiv:2311.16665 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16665

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2023). “Although this conjecture is still open, we know that many graph properties can be deduced from the deck.”

record.title: The PL action conjecture for dagger $(infty,n)$-categories
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{AdjCat}_{(\infty,n)}$ be the $(\infty,1)$-category of $(\infty,n)$-categories with adjoints, and let $\mathrm{PL}(n)$ denote the group of piecewise-linear self-equivalences of $n$-dimensional diagrams. Write $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf{AdjCat}_{(\infty,n)})$ for the space of automorphisms of this category.

**PL action conjecture.** There is a natural map

$$
\mathrm{PL}(n) \to \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbf{AdjCat}_{(\infty,n)}).
$$

This map is an equivalence.

The conjecture formalizes the expected graphical calculus for $(\infty,n)$-categories with adjoints: piecewise-linear transformations of diagrams should induce, and exhaust, the automorphisms of the associated interpreter category. Its status is not established in the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Giovanni Ferrer, Brett Hungar, Theo Johnson-Freyd, Cameron Krulewski, Lukas Müller, Nivedita, David Penneys, David Reutter, Claudia Scheimbauer, Luuk Stehouwer and Chetan Vuppulury, “Dagger n-categories”, arXiv:2403.01651 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01651

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for graph genus distributions
record.statement: For a graph $G$ and a nonnegative integer $g$, let $a_g(G)$ denote the number of $2$-cell embeddings of $G$ in an orientable surface of genus $g$, counted up to combinatorial homeomorphism equivalence. The sequence $(a_0(G),a_1(G),a_2(G),\dots)$ is the genus distribution of $G$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The genus distribution of every graph $G$ is unimodal. The paper notes that although the log-concavity conjecture has counterexamples, the genus distributions in those examples remain unimodal; the conjecture is presented as a plausible weakening and remains open.
record.source_name: Bojan Mohar, “Strong log-convexity of genus sequences”, arXiv:2405.10854 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10854

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2024). “This conjecture is reminiscent to the Heron–Rota–Welsh Log Concavity Conjecture that was recently resolved in the affirmative by June Huh et al. , except that it is closer to the notion of $\Delta$-matroids than to the usual matroids.”

record.title: Density-realization conjecture for weak saturation limits
record.statement:
Let $\delta\geq2$ be fixed, and let $w\in\mathbb Q\cap[\delta/2,\delta-1]$. **Density-realization conjecture.** There exists a graph $F$ such that

$$
\delta_F=\delta\qquad\text{and}\qquad w_F=w.
$$

This would extend the dense-range realization theorem in the paper from the cases established there; the source presents it as another problem for future research, so the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Ruben Ascoli and Xiaoyu He, “Rational values of the weak saturation limit”, arXiv:2501.15686 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15686

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

record.title: Scaling conjecture for longest subsequences in uniform separable permutations and cographs
record.statement:
Let $calpha(1/2)$ and $X(1/2)$ be the exponent and limiting random variable from the Brownian separable permuton result. Let $coverline{\sigma}_n$ and $coverline{G}_n$ be, respectively, a uniform separable permutation and a uniform separable cograph of size $n$.

**Uniform separable scaling conjecture.** There is a deterministic constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{LIS}(\overline{\sigma}_n)}{n^{\alpha(1/2)}} \xrightarrow[n\rightarrow \infty]{\mathrm{d}} c \cdot X(1/2)
$$

and

$$
\frac{\operatorname{LIN}(\overline{G}_n)}{n^{\alpha(1/2)}} \xrightarrow[n\rightarrow \infty]{\mathrm{d}} c\cdot X(1/2).
$$

The conjecture extends the Brownian separable permuton and cograph results to uniform models; numerical simulations suggest $c\approx 0.901$, and the source notes that this is more precise than an earlier conjecture.
record.source_name: Arka Adhikari, Jacopo Borga, Thomas Budzinski, William Da Silva and Delphin Sénizergues, “The longest increasing subsequence of Brownian separable permutons”, arXiv:2506.19123 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19123

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

record.title: Turán's conjecture for complete 3-uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $K_k^{(3)}$ be the complete $k$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $\pi(K_k^{(3)})$ denote its Turán density.

**Turán's conjecture.** For any integer $k\geqslant 4$, we have

$$
\pi(K_k^{(3)})=1-\left(\frac{2}{k-1}\right)^2.
$$

This is a central open problem in extremal hypergraph theory; the exact Turán density is known only for a few small values of $k$.
record.source_name: Mingze Li, Jie Ma and Mingyuan Rong, “Recent advances in arrow relations and traces of sets”, arXiv:2507.23375 (2025).
record.references:
**18 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2507.16622](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16622), [arXiv:2303.00375](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00375), [arXiv:2303.00427](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00427), [arXiv:2209.04894](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.04894), [arXiv:2206.03948](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03948), [arXiv:2205.08474](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08474), [arXiv:2107.09233](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09233), [arXiv:1911.07969](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07969), [arXiv:1802.03648](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03648), [arXiv:1709.01590](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.01590), [arXiv:1601.07809](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.07809), [arXiv:1508.01784](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01784), and 5 more.

record.title: Alon–Spencer conjecture on non-star-forest intersection families
record.statement:
A graph is a **star-forest** if each of its connected components is a star. For a graph $H$, an $H$-intersecting family on $K_t$ is a family of subgraphs of $K_t$ such that the edge intersection of any two members contains a copy of $H$.

**Alon–Spencer conjecture.** There exists some constant $\epsilon > 0$ such that if $H$ is a fixed graph that is not a star-forest and $\mathcal F$ is an $H$-intersecting family on $K_t$, then

$$
|\mathcal F| < \left(\frac 12 - \epsilon\right)2^{\binom t2}.
$$

This conjecture predicts a uniform improvement over the one-half density for intersecting families whenever $H$ is not a star-forest. The source presents the claim as a more general conjecture connected to the proposed optimality of the Christofides bound; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Paul Hamrick and Gary Hu, “Lower Bounds on Intersection Families for Certain Graphs”, arXiv:2510.18064 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2310.18163](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18163).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18064

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2025). “In 2012, Christofides disproved this conjecture, using the graph shown in Figure .”

record.title: Derrida's conjecture for the critical resistance scaling constant
record.statement:
Let $R_n$ be the resistance in the critical resistance model, let $p_c=\frac12$, and let $c_{\mathrm{eff}}$ be the constant in the critical scaling conjecture for $\log R_n$. **Derrida's conjecture.** The preceding conjecture should hold with

$$
c_{\mathrm{eff}}=9\zeta(3),\qquad \zeta(3)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^3}.
$$

This is a refinement of the Addario-Berry et al. prediction, specifying its otherwise undetermined scaling constant; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Xinxing Chen, Thomas Duquesne and Zhan Shi, “Hipster random walks, random series-parallel graph and random homogeneous systems”, arXiv:2511.16880 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16880

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Logarithmic clique-width for cyclic box graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let ${\cal P}$ be a monotone partition of $V(G)$ into cliques. Assume that the box graph $b(G;{\cal P})$ is a chordless cycle. **The logarithmic cyclic-box conjecture.** There exists a function $g$ such that

$$
\operatorname{cwd}(G)\leq g(k)\log |V(G)|.
$$

The preceding forest result shows a constant clique-width bound when the box graph is acyclic, while this conjecture predicts a logarithmic bound when it is a single chordless cycle. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Chính T. Hoàng, Ramin Javadi and Nicolas Trotignon, “On the structure of (4K_1, C_4, P_6)-free graphs”, arXiv:2511.23195 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.23195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: Elphick–Linz–Wocjan conjecture on the positive spectral sum
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and clique number $omega$. Let $s^+(G)$ denote the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$. **Elphick–Linz–Wocjan conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\sqrt{s^+(G)} \leq n\left(1-\frac{1}{\omega}\right).
$$

The conjecture is known for weakly perfect graphs, Kneser graphs, triangle-free graphs and random graphs; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: M. Rajesh Kannan, Hitesh Kumar and Shivaramakrishna Pragada, “Localization of spectral Turán-type theorems”, arXiv:2512.01409 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01409

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Cycle-space spanning conjecture for highly connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, where $n$ is odd. Write $\kappa(G)$ for its vertex-connectivity, $\alpha(G)$ for its independence number, $\mathcal{C}(G)$ for its cycle space, and $\mathcal{C}_n(G)$ for the subspace spanned by the Hamilton cycles of $G$. **Cycle-space spanning conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, whenever

$$
\kappa(G) \geq c\alpha(G),
$$

we have

$$
\mathcal{C}_n(G)=\mathcal{C}(G).
$$

This conjecture removes the logarithmic connectivity condition required by the theorem proved in the source. It remains open, while the source establishes the conclusion under stronger conditions involving $\max\\{\alpha(G),\log n\\}$ or $\alpha(G)^2$.
record.source_name: Dan Hefetz and Michael Krivelevich, “On graphs whose cycle space is spanned by their Hamilton cycles”, arXiv:2606.05835 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05835

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
